thread:
incident-bot: 🚨 Pager alert: high error rate and >200ms p50 for private connections in Azure Norway East affecting on-prem customers. Paging oncall: @Jordan

Jordan: Acknowledged. I'm on it, grabbing initial metrics. Which customers are on the Norway East ExpressRoute?

Elena: a couple of enterprise Dedicated customers and 2 Private deployments with static routes -> onprem via ExpressRoute. Support ticket #CS-4981 opened.

Priya: Saw spike in BGP churn around 11:05 UTC, routes to our vnet egress preferring a new path reported by Azure. Could be BGP metric flip.

Jordan: Running quick traceroute from one private node to customer onprem endpoint:
```
traceroute to 10.10.5.1 (10.10.5.1), 30 hops max
 1  10.240.0.1  0.7 ms 0.6 ms 0.6 ms
 2  100.64.0.1  2.3 ms 2.1 ms 2.2 ms
 3  52.114.23.1  45.6 ms 46.1 ms 45.9 ms
 4  * * *
 5  80.65.190.2  190.1 ms 189.9 ms 190.4 ms
```

Jordan: packet loss and a big latency jump after hop 3.

Sam: I pulled BGP logs from our virtual router in the region — we see flapping on the egress prefix 198.51.100.0/24, AS path changed to include a transit that increases AS path length and preference. Looks like an upstream partner announced a more-specific override.

Priya: Confirmed. Azure reported a partial route redistribution from partner ASN 64521 -> new path with lower MED temporarily. This explains traffic path change.

Elena: Customer impact: CS reports increased request timeouts for inference in Private mode, errors ~12% for calls routed via Norway East. Non-Private hosted instances unaffected.

Jordan: Immediate mitigation ideas: 1) Withdraw BGP next-hop on our side to force failover to secondary region. 2) Add a more-specific route back. 3) Ask Azure NOC to prep a community/med update with partner. Which is least risky?

Priya: 1) will cause transient reconverge but should move traffic to backup region (West Europe). 2) requires coordination with onprem; risk of route leak if done incorrectly. 3) requires partner/Azure action and will take longer. I'd do 1) with short maintenance window and monitor. :thumbsup:

Jordan: Ok doing controlled withdraw on one router to steer test prefix, not blanket withdraw. Applying now (rollback ready).

deploy-bot: @Jordan executed command on vrouter-norwayeast-rt01: `bgp withdraw 198.51.100.0/24 test` — queued

Jordan: Withdraw applied. Monitoring metrics.

Priya: Metrics: p50 down from 220ms -> 60ms over next 60s, error rate drops to 3%. Traces show path via West Europe now.

Elena: Notifying affected accounts > sent email to account owners with summary and temporary mitigation.

Sam: Leaving a sticky note: need runbook change to automate controlled withdraw + rollback threshold. Filing infra ticket INFRA-1122.

Jordan: Handoff in 30m to Priya for night coverage. I'll update postmortem draft with timeline.

Priya: Taking over monitoring. Will coordinate with Azure on getting partner to correct BGP advertisement and request MED correction.

incident-bot: Action required: create incident record and pin timeline — incident record ID INC-2024-347 pinned by Jordan

Jordan: Quick customer note to CS — the mitigation steered traffic to West Europe; we expect normal behavior but will keep route pinned until partner resolves announcement.

Elena: CS updated customers with ETA 4h for upstream fix, asked for confirmation when stable.

Sam: Post-incident tasks: 1) add BGP alert for AS path changes + MED volatility 2) automate controlled withdraw (INFRA-1122) 3) update runbook with exact commands used 4) coordinate with partners on BGP filtering.

Priya: Marking as mitigated at 1718965599. Will keep watch and reopen if we see reappearance. :white_check_mark:

Jordan: Thanks all. Filing a short blameless RCA draft and assigning owners.

Elena: Good job triaging quickly. Leaving this thread for postmortem notes. :coffee:
